dedupe_keys.name: doe global energy storage database gesdb sandia national laboratories

description: The DOE Global Energy Storage Database is a project-level inventory of grid-connected energy storage installations worldwide, maintained by Sandia National Laboratories for the US Department of Energy. The current version was redesigned from an Excel template into a MongoDB-backed site with layered project records, interactive statistics and a policy subpage that so far covers the United States. Coverage: global; each project record holds applications (bulk energy, ancillary services, transmission and distribution deferral, resilience and back-up power, microgrids), location with latitude and longitude, announced, constructed, commissioned and decommissioned dates, grid interconnection level and ISO or RTO, technology, service providers, ownership, capital and operating cost, funding sources, and subsystem specifications (storage capacity, round-trip efficiency, charge and discharge power, ramp rate, response time, ride-through). The number of projects was not read. Format and access: searchable web table with per-project export to JSON or CSV, statistics charts and a map on gesdb.sandia.gov; free, after accepting a download agreement. Licence: the terms of use say that data created by or for DOE are public domain, while the site's arrangement and selection belong to NTESS; the download agreement forbids redistributing repackaged versions and asks that works using the data be displayed publicly. Caveats: the site says the data are still being validated and locations may be approximate; a Python API is announced but not yet released. Simulation uses: storage fleet inputs for capacity planning, flexibility and resilience studies. Related records: storage appears in the openTEPES expansion model (model-opentepes).
